events.title: The Sack of Rome and the stand of the Swiss Guard
events.shortBlurb: A mutinous imperial army stormed Rome, and the Pope's Swiss Guard died almost to a man defending him…
body: On 6 May 1527 the unpaid, mutinous army of the Emperor Charles V, Spanish tercios and German landsknechts, many of them Lutherans, stormed the walls of Rome. Their commander, the Duke of Bourbon, fell dead in the first assault, and some twenty thousand leaderless soldiers gave the city over to a sack that raged for days, followed by months of occupation.

Churches were plundered, relics and tombs desecrated, priests and nuns and citizens slain or held for ransom; thousands perished, and the population of Rome fell to a fraction of what it had been. Christendom took the catastrophe as a judgment of God, and the splendor of High Renaissance Rome never wholly returned.

At the Vatican the Swiss Guard, 189 men under Captain Kaspar Röist, made its stand by the obelisk and the steps of St. Peter's while Clement VII escaped by the covered corridor of the Passetto to Castel Sant'Angelo. Of the guard 147 fell, Röist among them; in memory of that stand the new recruits of the Pontifical Swiss Guard are sworn in each year on 6 May.
